rfi.title: EU lawmakers sign off on long-awaited US tariff deal
rfi.description: The European Parliament gave the green light on Tuesday to a tariff deal with the United States, in a bid to close a volatile chapter of transatlantic trade relations.

rfi.title: Mbappé breaks records as France see off spirited Senegal
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé scored twice as France launched their bid for a third World Cup crown with a 3-1 victory over Senegal in Group I on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Ghana boss Queiroz hails spirit of players ahead of Panama clash at World Cup
rfi.description: Ghana head coach Carlos Queiroz praised his players willingness to be flexible to different ideas as they went through their final preparations for their opening game at the 2026 World Cup against Panama on Wednesday in Toronto.

rfi.title: France powers ahead in AI development, with more funding, public service tools
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Tuesday a further investment of €655 million to accelerate the development of artificial intelligence as well as an AI programme for public service employees. France is keen to build strategic autonomy in the face of competition from China and the United States.

rfi.title: Over a billion children exposed to three or more climate hazards UN report shows
rfi.description: More than one billion children face at least three overlapping climate hazards, the UN childrens' agency Unicef has warned, while highlighting the disproportionate impact in some regions of the world.

rfi.title: G7 summit opens full day of talks with Ukraine, Iran and Trump tensions in focus
rfi.description: As the G7 summit enters its first full day of discussions, French President Emmanuel Macron faces the challenge of keeping his US counterpart Donald Trump engaged as leaders weigh pressure on Russia, Middle East diplomacy and renewed trade tensions with Washington.

rfi.title: France shuts down dozen Israeli stands at defence trade show
rfi.description: A dozen Israeli company stands were shut down Monday at a major international defence and security exhibition held outside Paris, sparking outrage from authorities in Israel.

rfi.title: Child sexual abuse commission urges France to speed up reforms
rfi.description: Only a third of the recommendations made more than two years ago by France's Independent Commission on Incest and Sexual Violence Against Children (Ciivise) have been fully implemented, the body said in an assessment submitted to the government.

rfi.title: Tunisia football chiefs call in Renard to take charge of World Cup campaign
rfi.description: Hervé Renard took over the Tunisia national squad on Tuesday for the remainder of their World Cup campaign following the departure of head coach Sabri Lamouchi who was in charge when the team lost 5-1 to Sweden

rfi.title: Fearsome France begin World Cup wary of over-confidence
rfi.description: France come into this year's World Cup as one of the leading contenders for the trophy having reached the final of the last two editions, but Tuesday's opponents in their opening game, Senegal, serve as a warning of the dangers of over-confidence.

rfi.title: Former CAR leader Bozizé on trial over crimes against humanity
rfi.description: A UN-backed court in the the Central African Republic will on Tuesday begin the trial in absentia of former president François Bozizé, over crimes against humanity committed between 2009 and 2013.

rfi.title: Journalists disappear as intimidation grips Mozambique's Cabo Delgado region
rfi.description: Almost a decade after an Islamist insurgency erupted in Mozambique's northern Cabo Delgado province, few reports on the conflict are emerging from the region. This third instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – hears from journalists and activists facing intimidation and violence.

rfi.title: France's Macron warns Iran against imposing Hormuz tolls
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday warned Iran against imposing tolls on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, saying "everything" should be done so fees are not charged for passage through the key bottleneck.

rfi.title: US and Iran reach deal to end war, reopen Hormuz
rfi.description: The United States and Iran said they reached a deal to end the Middle East war on all fronts including Lebanon, and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz, but offered little indication on the thorny question of Tehran's nuclear programme.

rfi.title: NGO warns Ebola epidemic is 'outpacing' response efforts in DRC
rfi.description: French NGO Doctors Without Borders warned Monday that "dangerous gaps" remain in efforts to rein in an Ebola outbreak that has killed more than 180 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Since the first reported cases a month ago, the virus has spread rapidly, with the situation now critical in Ituri province.

rfi.title: ‘No blank cheque' for president or government says Senegal’s Sonko
rfi.description: In his first major international interview since becoming Speaker of Senegal's National Assembly, former prime minister Ousmane Sonko talks to RFI and sister channel France 24 about his split with his long-time ally President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. In the wide-reaching discussion, he also touches on the debt crisis, homosexuality legislation, regional security, his political aspirations and the World Cup.

rfi.title: First contact: Cape Verde's rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Cape Verde will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the third instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the second smallest nation after Curaçao to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: Macron leads effort to bridge divides with Trump at France's G7 summit
rfi.description: As a G7 summit opens in eastern France on Monday, President Emmanuel Macron is set to lead the allies' efforts to narrow differences with the United States on Iran, Ukraine, trade and big tech regulation.

bbc.title: Tehran selling deal with US as victory – but for Iranians it was necessity
bbc.description: For many Iranians, the question is not whether the deal means victory, but whether it lowers prices and reduces fear of another war.

bbc.description: Many Lebanese remain doubtful that the agreement could finally mean the end of the fighting between Israel and Hezbollah.

bbc.title: Cuba tourism collapses as US pressure campaign bites
bbc.description: The number of foreign visitors is down by 58% compared to last year, Cuban officials say, amid sanctions and an effective oil blockade.

bbc.title: Somaliland opens Jerusalem embassy after Israel's recognition of its independence
bbc.description: The move comes six months after Israel became the first country to recognise the breakaway East African state.

bbc.title: Hungary's MPs block return of Orbán, limiting rule of PM to eight years
bbc.description: The vote fulfils a promise by new PM Péter Magyar to stop his predecessor from becoming prime minister again.

bbc.title: Group planned to attack White House UFC event using snipers and drones, FBI says
bbc.description: In newly unsealed court filings, the government says the group allegedly expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centres.

bbc.title: India temporarily bans Telegram over exam paper leak concerns

bbc.title: California's Gavin Newsom alleges justice department is investigating his wife and ex-staff
bbc.description: A source familiar with the investigations says they had been ongoing for "roughly a year".

bbc.title: Three reasons ships are not going through the Strait of Hormuz yet
bbc.description: Experts say that there are significant obstacles preventing  traffic from returning to the levels seen before the conflict began – security, mines and tolls.

Almost every child, including those from high-income countries, is now exposed to at least one hazard

Globally, children face increasing threats from heatwaves, storms, floods and droughts as the climate crisis worsens, with more than one billion facing at least three of these at once.

lemonde.title: France-Sénégal : Kylian Mbappé détrône Olivier Giroud et devient, à 27 ans, le meilleur buteur de l’histoire de l’équipe de France
lemonde.description: Auteur d’un doublé, mardi contre le Sénégal, ses 57ᵉ et 58ᵉ buts sous le maillot bleu, le capitaine des Bleus a effacé des tablettes son ancien coéquipier lors de la victoire de l’équipe de France (3-1) pour son entrée en lice à la Coupe du monde 2026.

lemonde.title: La vague de chaleur qui déferle sur la France, une deuxième flambée des températures « exceptionnelle » avant le début de l’été
lemonde.description: De jeudi à dimanche, de très fortes chaleurs et des nuits tropicales toucheront une large partie du pays, avec 34 °C à 38 °C du Sud-Ouest au Nord-Est, en passant par l’Ile-de-France. Les autorités sanitaires appellent à la prudence, notamment à l’occasion de la Fête de la musique, dimanche.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : l’Iran menace Israël d’une « réponse sévère » après les attaques au Liban qui ont fait quatre morts, mardi
lemonde.description: Malgré l’annonce d’un accord entre les Etats-Unis et l’Iran incluant la guerre opposant Israël au Hezbollah, mouvement pro-iranien, des attaques de drones ont visé deux véhicules dans la localité de Mayfadoun et un autre dans la ville voisine de Choukine, dans la région de Nabatiyé, selon l’Agence nationale de l’information.

lemonde.title: Autonomie de la Corse : le projet de réforme constitutionnelle arrive à l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Première étape d’un parcours législatif qui s’annonce incertain, le projet de loi constitutionnelle « pour une Corse autonome au sein de la République » doit être discuté en séance publique à l’Assemblée nationale, à partir du mardi 16 juin.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, G7 à Evian : Moyen-Orient, Ukraine, IA... retrouvez les principales déclarations des dirigeants
lemonde.description: Les dirigeants du G7, réunis à Evian en présence de Volodymyr Zelensky, ont signalé mardi leur volonté commune d’intensifier la pression sur Moscou pour arrêter la guerre en Ukraine. La situation au Moyen-Orient et l’accord entre l’Iran et les Etats-Unis ont aussi fait l’objet de discussions, en présence notamment de l’émir du Qatar et du président des Emirats arabes unis.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les tirs de la frégate russe sur un yacht britannique dans la Manche sont un incident « isolé », conclut Londres
lemonde.description: Les tirs du navire russe « visaient à prévenir une éventuelle collision », a déclaré, dans la soirée de mardi, le ministère de la défense britannique, qui avait lancé une enquête. Selon Moscou, les coups de semonce ont été tirés alors que le yacht dérivait « dangereusement » vers la frégate militaire.

lemonde.title: Sandra Hoibian, directrice générale du Crédoc : « Contrairement aux relations humaines, l’IA émotionnelle ne juge pas, ne trahit pas, ne contredit pas »
lemonde.description: D’après une étude du Centre de recherche pour l’étude et l’observation des conditions de vie, un quart des moins de 40 ans déclarent entretenir une relation amicale ou amoureuse avec une intelligence artificielle. La directrice générale de l’organisme explique, dans un entretien au « Monde », qu’à la bataille de l’attention va succéder celle de l’attachement.

lemonde.title: Canicule à Paris : la baignade autorisée dès mercredi dans le canal Saint-Martin
lemonde.description: Alors qu’un nouvel épisode caniculaire arrive, Paris expérimente l’ouverture anticipée du canal Saint-Martin à la baignade surveillée. A l’été, la Ville doit ouvrir une dizaine de sites de baignade surveillés – dont trois dans la Seine.

lemonde.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro, fils de l’ex-président brésilien, condamné à quatre ans de prison pour son lobbying auprès de Washington
lemonde.description: L’ancien député, installé aux Etats-Unis, avait poussé Donald Trump à prendre des sanctions économiques contre le Brésil afin d’influer sur le procès de son père devant la Cour suprême brésilienne.

lemonde.title: Un assistant IA capable « d’agir » : comment OpenAI voit l’avenir de ChatGPT
lemonde.description: La start-up d’intelligence artificielle a évoqué, mardi 16 juin, en lever de rideau du salon Vivatech, à Paris, le rapprochement prochain de deux de ses services, ChatGPT et Codex. Une réponse à la concurrence, notamment, de son rival Anthropic.

lemonde.title: 1er-Mai : le Sénat adopte le projet de loi donnant le droit aux boulangers et aux fleuristes de travailler
lemonde.description: Le texte prévoit que les artisans boulangers-pâtissiers et fleuristes puissent faire travailler leurs salariés ce jour-là, sous réserve qu’un accord de branche fixe les conditions de recueil de leur volontariat et de leur rémunération.

lemonde.title: Renault franchit un cap dans ses ambitions pour le secteur de la défense
lemonde.description: Le constructeur automobile a annoncé, mardi, un accord avec Thales pour commencer à produire en France, à partir de 2027, une munition téléopérée. Il s’agit du troisième partenariat de Renault dans la défense.

lemonde.title: Le préfet des Bouches-du-Rhône impose à la Métropole Aix-Marseille-Provence de couper 53 millions d’euros dans les aides aux communes
lemonde.description: Chargé de boucler le budget 2026 de l’établissement public, Jacques Witkowski choisit d’amputer les attributions de compensation. Des financements considérés comme « indus », mais qu’une partie des maires jugent intouchables.

lemonde.title: Soudan : « Le manque de moyens dans les camps de déplacés a rendu la vie insoutenable »
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », Marie-Hélène Verney, représentante du Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés à Khartoum, souligne que « les affrontements n’ont jamais vraiment cessé », avec « des attaques systématiques de drones, touchant de manière indiscriminée des cibles militaires et civiles ».

lemonde.title: « Toy Story 5 » : quand Pixar s’endort
lemonde.description: Alors que l’intelligence artificielle galope à vitesse exponentielle, le studio Pixar, autrefois formidable diplomate entre l’humanité et le numérique, n’a plus grand-chose à articuler ou proposer en la matière.

lemonde.title: Périscolaire à Paris : pourquoi un ex-animateur de l’école élémentaire Titon a été relaxé d’accusations de harcèlement sexuel sur des élèves de CM1
lemonde.description: Nicolas G. avait comparu, le 5 mai, à huis clos, pour des propos déplacés et des câlins appuyés imposés à neuf élèves de 10 ans, ainsi que pour agression sexuelle sur trois d’entre elles. Le tribunal a prononcé sa relaxe, mardi 16 juin.

france24fr.title: Brésil : Eduardo, un des fils Bolsonaro, écope de quatre ans de prison pour lobbying pour son père
france24fr.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro a été condamné à quatre ans de prison mardi au Brésil pour son lobbying auprès des autorités américaines afin qu'elles intercèdent auprès de son père, l'ancien président Jair Bolsonaro, lui-même condamné pour tentative de coup d'État. Il était notamment accusé d'avoir poussé les États-Unis de Donald Trump à des sanctions économiques contre le Brésil.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les supporters français célèbrent la victoire des Bleus face au Sénégal
france24fr.description: La France l'a emporté 3-1 face au Sénégal ce mardi lors de son premier match de poule. À Paris, les supporters sont ravis et rêvent déjà à la suite de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026: Les sénégalais déçus après la défaite mais confiants pour la suite
france24fr.description: Battu 3-1 par la France malgré une première période encourageante, le Sénégal a manqué de réalisme dans les moments clés. À Dakar, les supporters des Lions réagissent entre déception et espoir pour la suite de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : Mbappé dépasse Giroud, quels records sont les suivants ?
france24fr.description: Face au Sénégal, Kylian Mbappé a marqué mardi son 58e but en équipe de France, dépassant Olivier Giroud en tant que meilleur buteur de l'histoire des Bleus. Et le capitaine tricolore pourrait ne pas s'arrêter là. Tour d'horizon des records qu'il pourrait égaler ou dépasser lors de la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Foot : Mbappé continue d'écrire l'Histoire des Bleus
france24fr.description: Depuis la première édition de la Coupe du monde en 1930, l'équipe de France occupe une place à part dans l'histoire du football mondial. En effet, les Tricolores sont l’une des rares nations à avoir participé à la toute première compétition internationale de football, organisée en Uruguay. Pour autant, la France n'était pas encore une nation de football.

france24fr.title: La Réunion : le Parlement adopte une loi de réparation pour les "enfants de la Creuse"
france24fr.description: Le Parlement français a adopté définitivement, mardi, une loi de réparation pour les "enfants de la Creuse", ces plus de 2 000 mineurs réunionnais arrachés à leurs terres et déplacés dans l'Hexagone entre 1962 et 1984. Le texte prévoit la création d'une commission pour la mémoire, l'institution d'une journée nationale d'hommage le 18 février et l'ouverture d'un droit à réparation sous forme d'allocation forfaitaire.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Ghanéen Thomas Partey, accusé de viol, ne jouera pas au Canada
france24fr.description: La justice canadienne a rejeté mardi le recours du gouvernement ghanéen qui tentait d'obtenir un visa pour le milieu de terrain Thomas Partey. Accusé de sept viols et d'une agression sexuelle au Royaume-Uni, le joueur s'est vu refuser l'entrée sur le territoire canadien, où le Ghana jouera mercredi son premier match du Mondial 2026 face au Panama.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : effusion de joie à Paris après la victoire des Bleus face au Sénégal
france24fr.description: Longtemps poussive et peu inspirée, la France a finalement réussi ses débuts en Coupe du monde en battant le Sénégal 3-1 grâce notamment à un doublé de Kylian Mbappé, nouveau recordman de buts en bleu. Les supporters qui assistaient au match depuis la fan zone de Paris ont célébré la victoire.

france24fr.title: En Haïti, le chef de l'ONU Antonio Guterres demande "pardon" aux victimes des gangs
france24fr.description: Lors d'une visite à Port-au-Prince mardi, le patron de l'ONU Antonio Guterres a présenté ses excuses aux Haïtiens pour "n'avoir pas été capable de mobiliser la communauté internationale" face à la violence des gangs qui gangrène le pays.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Qui est Vozinha, gardien héroïque du Cap Vert ?
france24fr.description: Le gardien Vozinha a été le ⁠héros du Cap-Vert ​lors du match nul contre l'Espagne lundi (0-0) pour le premier match de Coupe du monde de l'histoire de son pays. Il jouait à 40 ans son premier match dans un Mondial et a été désigné homme du match.

france24fr.title: Coupe du Monde 2026 : Mbappé et la France éteignent le Sénégal
Coupe du Monde 2026 : Mbappé et la France éteignent le Sénégal
france24fr.description: L'équipe de France a réussi son entrée en lice à la Coupe du monde 2026 en battant mardi le Sénégal (3-1). Si les Lions de la Teranga ont longtemps gardé les vice-champions du monde sous pression, ils n'ont rien pu faire lorsque les Bleus ont haussé le ton. Kylian Mbappé en a profité pour dépasser le record de buts de Giroud en sélection.

france24fr.title: Non, Kylian Mbappé n'a pas été harcelé par Emmanuel Macron
france24fr.description: Alors que la France joue ce mardi son premier match de Coupe du Monde, contre le Sénégal, de récentes publications sont revenues sur le départ de Kylian Mbappé du PSG vers le Real Madrid il y a 2 ans. Elles l'assurent : le capitaine des Bleus aurait quitté le club parisien du fait du comportement d'Emmanuel Macron. Explications d'une intox.

france24fr.title: France: les émissions de gaz à effet de serre baissent mais toujours pas assez
france24fr.description: Les émissions de gaz à effet de serre de la France ont baissé plus qu'attendu pour 2024 et 2025. Le CITEPA, l'organisme de surveillance des émissions française, a revu ses estimations mais prévient: pour atteindre l'objectif fixé en 2030, il faudra plus que doubler le rythme de cette baisse. D'autant qu'il ne s'agit que des émissions brutes, c'est à dire sans compter le CO2 capté par les forêts et sols. Nos puits de carbone s'épuisent et nous aident de moins en moins à compenser ces émissions.

france24fr.title: Un navire de guerre russe tire des coups de semonce dans la Manche
france24fr.description: Un yacht immatriculé au Royaume-Uni et naviguant dans la Manche au sud de l'île de Wight a signalé qu'un navire de guerre russe avait tiré près de lui des coups de semonce. Le ministère britannique de la Défense a lancé une enquête.

france24fr.title: Zelensky au G7 : Poutine sous pression ?
france24fr.description: Une réunion consacrée à l’Ukraine s’est tenue ce mardi lors du G7, en présence du président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky. Donald Trump a déclaré être prêt à rétablir les sanctions visant le pétrole russe et a estimé que la Russie "devrait conclure un accord" avec l'Ukraine. Les autres membres du G7 souhaitent également intensifier la pression sur Moscou afin de trouver une issue à la guerre.

france24fr.title: Bruno Fuchs (Les Démocrates) : "Trump s'est mis dans une tenaille"
france24fr.description: Alors que Donald Trump a annoncé dimanche soir la conclusion d’un accord avec l'Iran, le président de la commission des affaires étrangères de l'Assemblée nationale, Bruno Fuchs, estime que "la situation sera plus défavorable au monde qu'elle ne l'était". Concernant la situation au Liban, le député Les Démocrates privilégie "une vision politique et non pas militaire, qui est une impasse à long terme".

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026: les supporters sénégalais confiants avant France-Sénégal
france24fr.description: Le choc France-Sénégal, c'est ce mardi soir à partir de 19h GMT. Les deux sélections se connaissent bien. Les Lions avaient battu la France en 2002. À l'approche de la rencontre de ce soir, les supporters sénégalais affichent leur confiance et promettent une ambiance électrique autour des Lions de la Teranga.

zeit.description: Mehr als 5.000 Menschen sind im Jahr 2025 durch Minen getötet oder verletzt worden. Die UN wirbt dafür, Minen zu räumen und solche Waffen nicht mehr herzustellen.

zeit.description: Die USA und andere G7-Staaten erhöhen den Druck auf Russland, den Ukrainekrieg zu beenden. Geplant sind neue Öl- und Gassanktionen sowie Militärhilfe für die Ukraine.

zeit.description: Im Nebel ist eine britische Jacht nahe an ein russisches Kriegsschiff geraten. Dessen Reaktion sollte laut Russland und Großbritannien eine Kollision verhindern.

zeit.description: In der ersten Hälfte hat Frankreich gegen Senegal keine einzige nennenswerte Chance. Am Ende machen zwei Tore von Kylian Mbappé den Unterschied. Der Spielbericht

nzz.title: Independent Collectors by NZZ Art: Private Sammlungen, die eine Reise wert sind
nzz.description: Das weltweit führende Netzwerk für private Sammlungen zeitgenössischer Kunst bietet Zugang zu knapp 7000 Sammlungen aus rund 100 Ländern – wir stellen sechs Trouvaillen vor.

nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Impressionen der Fussball-WM 2026
nzz.description: Drei Gastgeber, 48 Teilnehmer: Vom 11. Juni bis zum 19. Juli findet die Fussball-Weltmeisterschaft der Männer in Mexiko, Kanada und den USA statt. Einblicke in die WM in Bildern.

nzz.title: Crans-Montana: Präsident Féraud wird an der ersten Gemeindeversammlung seit der Brandkatastrophe zum Rücktritt aufgefordert
nzz.description: Gut eine Stunde lang sprach die Versammlung über die schlimme Silvesternacht. Dann zeigte sich: Nicolas Féraud geniesst in der Gemeinde grossen Rückhalt, obwohl er im Strafverfahren beschuldigt wird.

nzz.title: Die SVP will mit Natalie Rickli und Martin Hübscher in den Zürcher Regierungsrat
nzz.description: Nach einigem hin und her hat die Partei entschieden, wer für die SVP in den Wahlkampf um Sitze in der Zürcher Regierung ziehen soll.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Pezeshkian bezeichnet das Rahmenabkommen als einen diplomatischen Sieg für Iran +++ USA und Iran wollen Deal auf dem Bürgenstock unterzeichnen
nzz.description: Seit April gilt eine Waffenruhe zwischen den USA, Israel und Iran. Doch in den vergangenen Tagen griffen sich die Staaten gegenseitig an. Die Folgen des Konflikts sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: Trumps Friedensshow erreicht Évian. Er entdeckt die Ukraine wieder
nzz.description: Folgt auf den Iran-Durchbruch nun auch Bewegung im festgefahrenen Konflikt zwischen Russland und der Ukraine? Beim G-7-Gipfel in Évian konnten sich die Staats- und Regierungschefs auf neue Sanktionen gegen Moskau einigen.

nzz.title: Russische Fregatte gibt im Ärmelkanal einen Warnschuss auf eine Jacht ab
nzz.description: Durch die Meerenge zwischen England und Frankreich fahren immer wieder russische Kriegsschiffe. Sollen sie die Schattenflotte beschützen?

nzz.title: SpaceX nutzt seinen Börsenboom und kauft das KI-Startup Cursor für 60 Milliarden Dollar
nzz.description: Der Raumfahrtpionier wird an der Börse von euphorischen Musk-Fans zu neuen Rekorden getragen. Er braucht aber Hilfe, damit er im Rennen um das beste KI-Modell gegen Anthropic und Google besteht.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Falschbehauptungen über Elon Musk und Arne Schönbohm: Das ZDF lernt nichts aus seinen Skandalen
nzz.description: Der Sender aus Mainz fällt immer wieder mit irreführenden Sendungen auf. Erst vergangene Woche warf er Musk ohne jeden Beleg vor, dieser rufe zu Menschenjagden auf. Die ideologische Schieflage hat beim ZDF System.

nzz.title: Magyars Abrechnung in Ungarn: Eine Amtszeitbegrenzung verunmöglicht Orbans Rückkehr an die Macht
nzz.description: Ungarns neuer Regierungschef Peter Magyar setzt mit dem forschen Vorgehen gegen das frühere Fidesz-Regime ein zentrales Wahlversprechen um. Die Art und Weise erinnert jedoch an Viktor Orban.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Das Treffen auf dem Bürgenstock ist für die Schweiz ein notwendiger Erfolg. Denn im Umgang mit Iran machte sie Fehler
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran wollen Ende Woche in der Zentralschweiz eine Absichtserklärung unterzeichnen. Das Aussendepartement sollte mit dem über Jahrzehnte aufgebauten Vertrauen sorgfältiger umgehen.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Viele Menschen glauben, Trump sei tatsächlich verrückt. Das ist auch ein Vorteil für ihn»
nzz.description: Donald Trump gilt als unberechenbar und impulsiv. Der britische Historiker James D. Boys erkennt darin eine Strategie aus dem Kalten Krieg. Der amerikanische Präsident inszeniere den Wahnsinn bewusst.

nzz.title: Aufhebung des AKW-Verbots: Der Ständerat unterstützt Bundesrat Rösti, gibt ihm aber Hausaufgaben auf
nzz.description: Ein Bericht, der bis Ende Jahr veröffentlicht wird, soll dem Energieminister eine Mehrheit im Parlament bringen und zeigen, wie neue Atomkraftwerke finanziert werden können.

nzz.title: Ein Uber-Fahrer soll in einem Auto eine betrunkene schlafende Frau geschändet haben. Er selbst erzählt vor Gericht eine andere Version
nzz.description: Die Frau trug eine Pulsuhr. Für die Vorinstanz waren deren Daten ein wichtiges Indiz für die Verurteilung.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Staatschefs, Tränengas und ein brennendes Auto: die Bilder des G-7-Gipfels – und der Anti-G-7-Demonstration in Genf
nzz.description: Vom 15. bis 17. Juni findet in Évian auf der französischen Seite des Genfersees der G-7-Gipfel statt. In Genf ist am Sonntag gegen die Veranstaltung demonstriert worden, teilweise mit Gewalt.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM: Adidas geht das V für DFB-Fan-Trikots aus
spiegel.description: Fans von Kai Havertz, Aleksandar Pavlović und Deniz Undav haben derzeit ein Problem: Adidas kann den Buchstaben V nicht auf Trikots flocken. Der DFB-Ausrüster liefert eine Erklärung – und einen Hoffnungsschimmer.

spiegel.title: Göttingen: 16-Jähriger stellt sich nach Schuss auf Polizisten
spiegel.description: Zwei Großfamilien waren aneinandergeraten, am Ende des Streits landete ein Göttinger Polizeibeamter angeschossen auf der Intensivstation. Nun hat sich ein Verdächtiger gemeldet – und seinen Anwalt gleich mitgebracht.

spiegel.title: Tödlicher Sturz von Brücke in Brasilien: Rätsel um verschwundene Kamera
spiegel.description: Eine junge Frau wird von einer Brücke ohne Sicherungsseil 40 Meter in den Tod geworfen. Nun berichtet ein Zeuge von einer Kamera, welche die Frau getragen haben soll. Das Gerät wurde bislang nicht gefunden.

spiegel.title: Boris Pistorius: Aktionsplan Drohnen soll Abwehr der Bundeswehr stärken
spiegel.description: Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius hat in Friesland einen »Aktionsplan Drohnen« angekündigt. Die Bundeswehr soll mit mehreren Milliarden Euro besser für Aufklärung, Einsatz und Abwehr gerüstet werden.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Michael Olise und Kylian Mbappé führen Frankreich zu Auftaktsieg
spiegel.description: In Hälfte eins schwächelte Frankreich gegen überraschend robuste Senegalesen. Nach der Halbzeit zeigte Michael Olise, warum »Les Bleus« auf seine Genialität angewiesen sind.

spiegel.title: G7-Gipfel in Évian: Merz setzt auf gemeinsames Vorgehen von Europa und USA in Ukraine-Frage
spiegel.description: Der deutsche Kanzler zeigt sich nach Gesprächen in Évian mit den G7-Staatschefs optimistisch: Europa und USA könnten gemeinsam auf ein Ende des Ukrainekriegs hinarbeiten. Er habe Trump »aufmerksam« zuhören sehen.

spiegel.title: Pizza Hut: Fast-Food-Kette wird verkauft
spiegel.description: Zuletzt entwickelte sich die Fast-Food-Kette zum Sorgenkind im Unternehmen: Yum Brands verkauft seine Pizza-Hut-Restaurants. Der Gastrokonzern streicht dafür Milliarden ein.

spiegel.title: Tom Holland und Zendaya: Haben sie bereits geheiratet? »Mehr als das wirst du dazu nicht erfahren«
spiegel.description: Tom Holland hat sich erstmals zu Gerüchten über eine Hochzeit mit Zendaya geäußert. Mit seinen Worten über die KI-generierten Hochzeitsbilder sorgte der Schauspieler erneut für Spekulationen.

spiegel.title: EU-Parlament stimmt für Verbot von KI für Missbrauch-Deepfakes
spiegel.description: Die EU geht gegen Anwendungen vor, mit denen sich manipulierte sexuelle Darstellungen produzieren lassen. Die Parlamentarier in Straßburg stimmten jetzt mit überwältigender Mehrheit für ein entsprechendes Verbot.

spiegel.title: Fall Fabian: Zeuge Olaf K. ging mit Gina H. zur Leiche
spiegel.description: Gina H. soll den achtjährigen Fabian erstochen haben. Als man den Jungen bereits suchte, fuhr sie mit zwei Männern zur Leiche. Was einer der beiden nun vor Gericht aussagte, klingt verstörend.

spiegel.title: Palantir: Frankreich beendet Zusammenarbeit mit US-Konzern
spiegel.description: Der französische Inlandsgeheimdienst will künftig nicht mehr das KI-Unternehmen Palantir nutzen. Stattdessen investiert die Regierung Millionen in eigene KI-Infrastruktur, um unabhängiger von US-Technologie zu werden.

spiegel.title: USA: Warum Franchises gerade so beliebt sind
spiegel.description: Chef statt Student: Immer mehr junge Menschen wollen Franchisenehmer großer Ketten werden. Auch, weil das Geschäft als KI-sicher gilt und längst mehr bietet als nur Fast-Food.

spiegel.title: Alaska-Wahl: Dan Sullivan darf nicht gegen Dan Sullivan antreten
spiegel.description: Bei den Midterm-Vorwahlen in Alaska wollte ein Mann antreten, der denselben Namen wie der aktuelle Senator trägt. Der Amtsinhaber witterte Wählertäuschung. Die Wahlbehörde hat den zweiten Dan Sullivan nun ausgeschlossen.

spiegel.title: BMW kappt Prognosen deutlich – Aktie fällt
spiegel.description: Der deutsche Autobauer BMW senkt wegen der Schwäche am chinesischen Automarkt und den Folgen des Nahostkonflikts seinen Jahresausblick. Die Auswirkungen zeigen sich auch an der Börse.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Russland baut ein eigenes Starlink. Wie gut ist das System?
spiegel.description: Elon Musk hat den Russen sein System verweigert. Nun behauptet Putin, die Arbeit am eigenen Satelliteninternet Rassvet schreite »zügig und in guter Qualität« voran. Doch es gibt Probleme.

spiegel.title: Shein: BHV Marais trennt sich nach Kritik vom chinesischen Modekonzern
spiegel.description: Nur Monate nach dem umstrittenen Einzug des chinesischen Modeunternehmens Shein trennt sich das Pariser Traditionskaufhaus BHV Marais von dem Onlinehändler. Das neue Management spricht von einem strategischen Fehler.

spiegel.title: Michel Friedman: Publizist kritisiert Absage von Gedenkfeier in Bayreuth
spiegel.description: Wegen vermeintlicher Sicherheitsbedenken wird eine Veranstaltung zur Aufarbeitung der Festspielgeschichte gestrichen. Der jüdische Autor Michel Friedman spricht von einem fatalen Signal für die Demokratie.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz und Donald Trump: Kanzler setzt beim G7-Gipfel auf Geschenk-Diplomatie
spiegel.description: Tag zwei beim G7-Gipfel: Neben Nahostkonflikt und Ukrainekrieg ging es auch darum, Donald Trump milde zu stimmen. Friedrich Merz überreichte dem US-Präsidenten sogar ein verspätetes Geburtstagsgeschenk. Sehen Sie selbst.

observador.title: Pode ignorar-se o sinal da pertença ?
observador.description: O actual Presidente nunca desistirá de atender, proteger, privilegiar os seus - mesmo que aqui e ali os atice ou desespere, nunca esquecerá porém o seu mandamento primeiro: ser amado por todos.

observador.title: Empresas, empresas e empresas
observador.description: Olhando de longe, parece-me que o ministro da Economia não está suficientemente focado nas empresas. Entendo perfeitamente que se preocupe com os fundos europeus e com o PRR. Mas o PRR é passageiro.

observador.title: O português que ganhou bilhete para o Mundial graças à voz
observador.description: A Seleção chegou a hotel InterContinental de Houston sob o apoio de centenas de adeptos. Francisco Vilarinho gritou o nome de todos os jogadores e ganhou um bilhete para o jogo de Portugal.

observador.title: Os reaccionários chocam contra a realidade
observador.description: A globalização e o comércio livre são, sem uma única excepção que valha a pena, o melhor motor de crescimento que a humanidade conhece, e o proteccionismo a forma mais fiável de o desligar.

observador.title: Zeros à esquerda fulos com zeros à direita do Elon
observador.description: Se Musk fosse decente, vendia tudo e dividia a fortuna pelo mundo. Causaria o colapso económico global, sim, mas não seriam 150€ a impedir uma criança em África de ir ao próximo concerto do Bad Bunny.

observador.title: 00h. Irão promete responder a ataques no Líbano
observador.description: Irão diz que vai responder de forma "severa" aos ataques israelitas no sul do Líbano. Ainda, Portugal já chegou a Houston para a estreia no Mundial.

observador.title: André Pardal e Luís Rodrigues avançam com lista conjunta
observador.description: A lista vai ser liderada pelo ex-deputado André Pardal, que no último Congresso liderou a terceira mais votada, e incluirá o antigo presidente da distrital de Setúbal Luís Rodrigues.

observador.title: Novos bombardeamentos russos provocam pelo menos oito mortos
observador.description: Em Nikopol, na região de Dnipropetrovsk (centro-leste), o exército russo atacou com drones civis que "circulavam ao longo de uma estrada", matando três pessoas.

observador.title: Encontrado corpo de jovem junto à barra de Albufeira
observador.description: A Polícia Marítima retirou o corpo para a marina de Albufeira, tendo sido realizado no local a verificação do óbito. O jovem desapareceu quinta-feira quando se encontrava a banhos na praia.

observador.title: "Coração apertado": César Peixoto despede-se do Gil Vicente
observador.description: "Enquanto profissional, tenho que dar este passo. Se fosse pelo coração, não daria", disse o treinador. César Peixoto sublinhou que continuará a acompanhar o percurso dos gilistas mesmo à distância.

observador.title: Futebol e casas portuguesas para quem pode (os americanos)
observador.description: Se nada mudar no nosso discurso público, então nem quando o Mundial de Futebol de 2030 for em Portugal os portugueses vão ter dinheiro para pagar os bilhetes.

observador.title: Pedrógão e o futuro: a gestão do fogo em "economês"
observador.description: Se quem tem uma visão Liberal da economia quer ajudar a manter o território a salvo de incêndios catastróficos, deve parar de desenhar realidades que não existem.

observador.title: A Saúde Escolar está infectada pela Ideologia de Género
observador.description: Então a DGS acha que as crianças entre os 3 e 6 anos de idade devem aprender sobre o corpo e autonomia, privacidade e consentimento, identidade, género e diversidade?

observador.title: Os que voltam
observador.description: Como é possível que um serviço de urgência se tenha tornado a sala de estar de tantas pessoas?

observador.title: Vamos lá ser felizes neste intervalo
observador.description: Vamos aproveitar porque a vida são dois dias e o mundial vai para lá de muitos.

observador.title: Sobre o aborto e preconceitos…
observador.description: A revolta contra os que se opõem a que o aborto seja uma prática aceitável dirige-se ao mensageiro quando, na verdade, o incómodo vem da mensagem em si.

observador.title: Ministro: reforma do Estado é chave da competitividade

new-sci.title: The secrets to keeping your brain sharp in old age
new-sci.description: Neurologist Emily Rogalski studies "superagers" – people in their 80s or 90s with unusually keen memories, whose lifestyles suggest ways to slow cognitive decline

new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: Technology is changing our perspective on nature – at every scale
new-sci.description: Inspired by Ariel Waldman’s docuseries Life Unearthed, columnist Annalee Newitz explores how microscopes, drones and specialised cameras are giving us an unprecedented view of nature from many different vantage points

new-sci.title: Has the answer to life's origins been hiding in our cells all along?
new-sci.description: The surprising discovery of mysterious blobs inside our cells is revolutionising our understanding of how life works, and how it got started

new-sci.title: The social media ban is an experiment – here’s how it will be studied
new-sci.description: Scientists have long grappled with how to measure the effect of social media on children. Now, the UK government has announced a total ban for everyone under 16, and researchers are rushing to design rigorous studies before it comes into effect

new-sci.title: Inside the start-up aiming for a giant leap in robot intelligence
new-sci.description: Physical Intelligence is drawing on the broad knowledge of large language models to help robots understand instructions and learn to carry out any task independently

new-sci.title: We may have finally solved cosmology's chicken-or-the-egg problem
new-sci.description: Galaxies and their supermassive black holes evolve together, but which came first is an ongoing question. Now we may finally have an answer, says columnist Leah Crane

new-sci.title: Are useful and error-free quantum computers only two years away?
new-sci.description: Quantum computing firm QuEra says it plans to make a fault-tolerant quantum computer and offer it to users through the cloud in 2028, which will require a real leap in engineering

new-sci.title: Why controversial ideas in science shouldn't always be dismissed
new-sci.description: Researchers suggesting that the keto diet could treat mental health conditions find themselves uncomfortably aligned with people like vaccine-sceptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr, but that is not a reason to reject the idea

new-sci.title: What is a ‘normal’ memory slowdown, and when should I worry?
new-sci.description: Lapses in memory are a normal part of ageing but can also be signs of dementia. Here’s how to distinguish between typical brain ageing and cognitive decline

new-sci.title: Understanding anorexia’s grip on the brain could unlock new therapies
new-sci.description: One-third of people with anorexia nervosa don’t recover and treatment has remained stagnant for years. Now we’re beginning to understand how the condition takes over the mind

new-sci.title: Sci-fi horror film Backrooms is a triumph for its 20-year-old director
new-sci.description: With its origins in a creepy image posted on 4chan, Backrooms is an unusually potent big-screen experiment in fear and perception, says Davide Abbatescianni

new-sci.title: Hundreds of new moons are revealing our solar system's violent history
new-sci.description: The outer solar system once seemed like a quiet backwater. But a glut of tiny, strange moons with unruly orbits are coming into view, revealing hints of a surprising past – and the origin of Saturn's rings

new-sci.title: The relationship recession is even bigger for Gen Z than we thought
new-sci.description: We know that members of Gen Z are less likely to be in a steady relationship than millennials were at their age, but previous research missed out an important factor that actually widens the relationship recession

phys-org.title: New method enables accurate sequencing of short peptides hidden in food and human body
phys-org.description: Our food and our bodies are full of tiny protein fragments called peptides. These small chains of amino acids act as biological messengers, influencing processes ranging from sensory perception to physiological functions.

phys-org.description: Marine heat waves (MHWs) are events characterized by prolonged warm coastal and ocean conditions with wide-ranging impacts on ecosystem health and associated industries. While research on MHWs has historically relied on surface-water data from satellite observations and buoy records, new research from the Batten School of Coastal & Marine Sciences & VIMS highlights the need to—quite literally—go deeper.

phys-org.description: Using artificial intelligence, scammers can duplicate someone's voice with just seconds of audio, says the University of Cincinnati's Kimberly Hyun. Impostor scams are one of the most common forms of fraud, according to the Federal Trade Commission.

phys-org.title: Intensive nickel mining has transformed microbial biodiversity of Thio Lagoon in New Caledonia
phys-org.description: A study carried out by scientists from Ifremer, IRD, the universities of Western Brittany (UBO) and Bordeaux, CNRS, and the University of Tartu (Estonia) reveals the impact of nickel mining on the coastal ecosystems of New Caledonia. phys-org.title: Webb and Hubble reveal the history of a relic of Milky Way's formation
phys-org.description: Researchers using two of humanity's most powerful observatories—NASA's James Webb and Hubble Space Telescopes—have definitively shown that Terzan 5 is not a globular star cluster, as it was once classified, offering new insight into how galaxies like our own form and evolve over time.

phys-org.title: Report reveals how digital tools are transforming biodiversity crisis response
phys-org.description: Scientists who study plant physiology and evolution have a new tool in their toolkit: a machine learning algorithm that can scan digital plant specimen collections and quickly measure leaf size and thickness.

phys-org.title: Cotton's roots traced to Yucatan Peninsula, where wild gene pool runs deepest
phys-org.description: There's nothing like this in nature, Jonathan Wendel said as he showed a visitor in his Bessey Hall office the long white puffs billowing from a cotton boll—the protective flower capsule of the plant cultivated by humans for thousands of years. In the wild, cotton bolls are far smaller and hold darker, coarser and shorter fibers.

phys-org.title: Santa Cruz trail study reveals how mountain lions and outdoor recreation can safely share spaces
phys-org.description: California's iconic Santa Cruz Mountains are an outdoor recreation wonderland. With a world-class network of hiking, mountain biking and equestrian trails, they draw millions of visitors each year from neighboring Santa Cruz, Santa Clara, San Francisco and San Mateo counties.

phys-org.title: Quantum hyperdimensional computing can work 500 times faster than other methods
phys-org.description: Cleveland Clinic researchers are unlocking quantum computing's full potential through the creation of a new computing paradigm inspired by the human brain. Fabio Cumbo, Ph.D., research associate in the lab of Daniel Blankenberg, Ph.D., associate staff, Computational Life Sciences, is developing the model, called quantum hyperdimensional computing (QHDC).

phys-org.title: New national publication gives teachers guidance on AI in the classroom
phys-org.description: With artificial intelligence tools available on every phone, laptop and tablet, higher education has struggled to implement consistent recommendations for how and when AI can be used. A new national guide seeks to change that.

phys-org.title: Random deformation lets glassy materials store precise mechanical memories, simulations reveal
phys-org.description: Amorphous materials such as glass are solids whose internal structure lacks a repeating pattern. Their molecules are arranged in a random and irregular way. Surprisingly, these disordered materials can "remember" past mechanical experiences; that is, the way they respond to a force can depend on how they have responded to external forces before.

phys-org.title: Cockatoos learn when touchscreen rewards 'die,' then apply rule to new contexts
phys-org.description: For humans, death is surrounded by culture, emotion, ritual and language. But the question can be framed in a much more basic way: What would an animal have to understand in order to recognize that someone has died?

phys-org.title: Politics in the logistics mix: How tariffs and polarization alter corporate supply chains
phys-org.description: How do political ideology and perceived ideological alignment influence supply chain professionals' evaluation of operational decisions involving politically charged macroeconomic issues such as tariffs?

phys-org.title: RNA barcoding approach reveals previously unknown virus–host relationships
phys-org.description: An interdisciplinary team of Rice University researchers has uncovered previously unknown relationships between bacteriophages—viruses that infect bacteria—and their bacterial hosts, offering a powerful new tool for next-generation microbiome engineering.

phys-org.title: Quantum lab aboard space station gets 'chilly' upgrade
phys-org.description: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station have switched on NASA's newly upgraded Cold Atom Lab, a one-of-a-kind facility designed to improve how scientists explore the fundamental workings of matter and develop new quantum technologies. By leveraging the unique environment of microgravity in space, the lab can accomplish cutting-edge science impossible to do anywhere else.

phys-org.title: AI system evaluates chemical spectra in minutes
phys-org.description: A research team has developed an artificial intelligence (AI) system that proposes suitable molecular structures from the raw data of spectroscopic measurements and assesses their plausibility. phys-org.title: A flexible graphene-based neural interface can 'speak and listen' to the brain
phys-org.description: Neural interfaces are devices that can detect or modulate neuronal activity when placed in contact with the brain. They are already used to treat various conditions related to the nervous system. However, current technologies still have limitations that can reduce their effectiveness. phys-org.title: AI-based system developed to better detect toxic online content
phys-org.description: A Concordia-led team of researchers has developed a new artificial intelligence-based method of detecting toxic online content that is faster and more accurate than existing tools. The system is designed to ensure social media platforms can reliably prevent user-generated content they deem harmful from appearing online.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Is All About Lebanon Now
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump says that he "calls the shots" on negotiating with Iran, and Israel has no choice but to submit to a deal that undermines its security interests. But a deal that makes Trump the protector of Lebanon—and, by extension, Iran-backed Hezbollah—could put the US and Israel on a collision course.

proj-syn.title: Every British Prime Minister’s Nightmare
proj-syn.description: The true nature of Britain’s “special relationship” with the United States has far more to do with American financiers’ willingness to keep borrowing to purchase British government debt than with history, culture, or Britain’s defense needs. Every UK Prime Minister must bear this burden, which is rapidly becoming unsustainable.

proj-syn.title: India’s Unfinished Reform Agenda
proj-syn.description: Elevated oil prices, potentially strong El Niño conditions during the monsoon season, and the tariff-induced fragmentation of global trade are bearing down on the Indian economy and will likely be a drag on GDP growth. But these adverse conditions may be a blessing in disguise if they force India to complete its economic reform agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Middle East’s New Normal
proj-syn.description: The most likely outcome of the Iran war is not peace but an unsatisfying ceasefire that leaves the underlying issues unresolved. This will mean an uneasy equilibrium in which Gulf countries go their own way, US influence wanes, and the regional order remains unsettled.

proj-syn.title: No Bridge Over Healing Waters for the G7
proj-syn.description: The French G7 presidency’s focus on global imbalances is both welcome and problematic. While long-standing trade imbalances between the United States, Europe, and China are, if anything, becoming even more troublesome, the leaders’ summit in Évian-les-Bains will do nothing to address the problem.

proj-syn.title: Are Government Stakes the Key to AI Sovereignty?
proj-syn.description: At first glance, reports that the US and Chinese governments are both considering taking stakes in national AI champions would seem to suggest a convergence between the world’s two leading AI powers. But a closer look reveals stark differences in their underlying strategies.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: Jefferson’s Revolutionary Language
proj-syn.description: Of the delegates who assembled in Philadelphia in 1776 for the Second Continental Congress, only Thomas Jefferson possessed the skill, knowledge, and linguistic gifts to make the Declaration of Independence an immortal text. He was the self-appointed conscience of America, and sensational imagery was his stock-in-trade.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of the Enslaved
proj-syn.description: For African-Americans, the Declaration of Independence was nothing but a “thin veil to cover the crimes” of slavery, as Frederick Douglass put it. Inspired by Haiti’s Declaration of Independence, free and enslaved Black people in the US found themselves subverting America’s founding document to achieve their own emancipation.

proj-syn.title: Free-Market Capitalism Is Destroying US Democracy
proj-syn.description: Far from two sides of the same coin, free-market capitalism and democracy are fundamentally incompatible. The only way to restore US democracy is to transform the system, so that it compensates innovators but limits their market power, while ensuring that the benefits of economic progress are more equitably shared.

proj-syn.title: Canada’s Great Recalibration
proj-syn.description: The growing fusion of economics, security, and technology has altered the nature of 21st-century interdependence, and Canada has responded by being more intentional. Rather than automatically serving as an extension of US-centered systems, it is creating more options across a wider network of relationships.

proj-syn.title: From Jefferson to Nehru
proj-syn.description: The Declaration of Independence continues to challenge countries, including the US and India, to measure themselves against the ideals they profess. But in a century marked by rising inequality, an authoritarian resurgence, and the emergence of new forms of domination, measuring up will become only more difficult.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Democratic Decline
proj-syn.description: Notwithstanding recent setbacks for illiberal, populist, and authoritarian leaders in some countries, good-governance groups and experts on democratic decline continue to document a disturbing global trend toward “autocratization.” What remains to be seen is whether enough voters will wake up to the threat.

proj-syn.title: The Standard of Independence
proj-syn.description: Although revolutions would surely have occurred had the United States never broken from Britain in 1776, the Declaration of Independence gave later anticolonial movements inspiration and the language to shape their own aspirations. It offered a universal blueprint, even as the US itself adopted the ethos of empire.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of Independence Turns South
proj-syn.description: Whether they were agreeing or arguing, the new countries that emerged across the Americas after the American Revolution influenced each other. Together, they helped shape the global development of modern democracy and the social and political movements that have shaped it ever since.

crunchbase.title: Rewriting Your Pitch: SaaS Isn’t Dead, But The Playbook For Founders Is Changing
